newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Amsterdam nine-month port traffic up 7.1 percent.
newsitem.headline: Amsterdam nine-month port traffic up 7.1 percent.

text.p: Amsterdam port area traffic rose 7.1 percent to 40 million tonnes in the first nine months of the year and is on course to better 1995's full-year record total of 50.3 million, the port authority said on Wednesday.
Shipments of dry bulk rose 6.7 percent on the same period last year to 26.5 million tonnes, with coal up 34.5 percent to 8.7 million tonnes and agribulk 6.7 percent higher at 6.5 million.
The port handled 7.6 million tonnes of liquid bulk, 0.7 percent more than last year. Oil products were up 0.1 percent to 5.5 million tonnes.

The general cargo sector rose 18.9 percent to almost six million tonnes with container shipments jumping 54.7 percent to 1.3 million tonnes, reflecting growth in traffic with West Africa and South America.
The ro-ro sector continued its decline, dropping 23.6 percent to 0.39 million tonnes.
The figures cover transhipments handled by the ports of Ijmuiden/Velsen, Beverwijk, Zaanstad and Amsterdam.
